Subject: Performance/SLO qualification — FinCo (context window, tokens, streaming)

Hi Alice — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we're aligned: 

Summary of FinCo targets you described:
- Peak traffic: ~120 requests/sec (spiky) with steady-state ~40–60 rps.
- Concurrent active sessions (streams): ~40–60 at peak.
- Typical prompt size: 2k tokens, but some use-cases send up to ~8k tokens of context (system + history + document).
- Expected generation: 256–1,024 tokens (most common ~512).
- Latency SLOs: p95 perceived latency (when streaming first token) target ~150ms; end-to-end completion p95 target <= 500ms (non-streamed acceptable for some back-office flows).
- Requirement: streaming for user-interactive chat to show first token quickly; some batch/async endpoints can accept higher completion latency.

Impact notes from our side (high level):
- Large context windows (4k–8k tokens) increase per-request memory and KV cache pressure, which reduces per-GPU throughput and raises tail latency for both first-byte and completion.
- For streaming-first-byte targets (~150ms p95), we typically recommend a streaming-optimized model variant and smaller quantization-friendly kernels; network + TLS handshake and serialization overhead matter at these scales.
- Throughput (rps) is primarily constrained by sequence length * total tokens (input + output) per request. So a steady 40 rps with 3k tokens/request yields much lower QPS than 40 rps at 512 tokens.

Proposed next steps from Redwood: 
1) We'll run a short benchmarking matrix for FinCo test profile: 2k-in/512-out, 4k-in/512-out, and 8k-in/512-out. We'll record p50/p95/p99 first-byte and completion latencies, and throughput at concurrency steps (10, 25, 50, 75).
2) We'll share the perf CSV and an initial SLA draft (attached) that maps to Dedicated pools / instance sizing recommendations.
3) If streaming first-byte is critical (150ms p95), we may recommend a dedicated pool with lower batch windows and a streaming-optimized runtime; we can demo a streaming-first token run.

Can you confirm the numbers above (peak rps, concurrency, context sizes) and whether the 150ms first-byte p95 is a hard requirement for all interactive paths or just the highest-priority flows? Once you confirm we’ll schedule the perf run and share results + recommended Dedicated capacity.

Thanks —
Marissa
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Hi Marissa — thanks for the clear recap. Numbers look right with two clarifications: 
1) Peak concurrency: we expect short spikes up to 60 concurrent active sessions (mostly due to campaign launches), so please run the 75 concurrency step you mentioned.
2) First-byte 150ms p95 is a hard requirement for our consumer chat product (the rest of the flows can accept 400–500ms p95 for completion).

We're also leaning toward a Dedicated pool for production due to data isolation and predictable latency — SOC2 is in our procurement checklist. Tom (copied) will own the security/compliance calls. 

Please find attached the traffic pattern PDF with hourly distribution and a sample user session log. Timeline: we'd like perf results and a recommended sizing doc by next Wednesday (2026-03-11) to inform procurement.

Appreciate it —
